changes: New socratic-tutor skill, adapted from Jane Street's agent_skills, teaches a topic to mastery by asking questions instead of lecturing. It places you with a short diagnostic, scores each subskill from 0 to 5 on a skill map, re-tests earlier subskills without warning, and ends with a final assessment. `save state` prints a block, or writes a file, that a new session can resume from.
entries.try: Tutor me on Postgres MVCC until I can explain it.

changes: teach now points requests to be quizzed or drilled to mastery at socratic-tutor, so "teach me" about a codebase still explains it and "tutor me" on a topic starts a session.

The Quality Director books a repo whose CI runs on local-ci. Set its `workflow` in `books/watched.csv` to `local-ci` and `fetch` reads the records local-ci publishes to the repo's `refs/local-ci/records` instead of Actions artifacts; `ingest` books them like any run, with `https://github.com/OWNER/NAME/commit/SHA#local-ci-STARTED` as the evidence. No job timings are booked for a local run, and the test volume book takes the week's commit from its newest local push.
entries.try: Point a local-ci repo's watch-list row at local-ci, then fetch, ingest and summarize its last week.

changes: `debrief.py check` no longer passes a VERIFIED claim whose `record` is a pathspec pattern such as `*`, `:(glob)**` or `:/`, or a folder, symlink or submodule: the record must name one regular file git tracks or has staged, exactly as `git ls-files` prints it. It also refuses to read a change record that is a symlink, sits outside the repo, or that git holds with a mode other than 100644, so a pull request can't make the check print another file's keys into its log or hang on a link to `/dev/zero`. A repo that pins debrief.py at an older commit gets this when its pin moves.

local-ci now keeps each run's test record for the quality books. A repo's `scripts/ci` that writes the record to `$LOCAL_CI_RECORD` (with `quality.py record-junit`, which `$QUALITY_PY` points at) has it published to the repo's `refs/local-ci/records` ref with a manifest local-ci writes itself: which commit, pull request or push, when, and the exit code. The ref is not a branch and starts no workflow. A failed push is retried on every tick and never changes the status.
entries.try: Make this repo's scripts/ci record its tests for local-ci and check the record lands on refs/local-ci/records.

changes: A `.changes/exempt` entry can now be a git glob, so a repo can exempt its dated weekly briefs (`briefs/[0-9]*.md`) and still ask for a change record when the brief template or a README beside them changes. A plain path matches as before. An entry has to name its top-level folder or file outright, so no pattern can exempt the whole repo (debrief 0.4.0).
entries.try: Which files in briefs/ does this repo's .changes/exempt let through without a change record?

changes: A repo can now enforce the change record check without failing its scheduled data pull requests. List the paths a weekly job writes, such as `briefs/` or `books/`, in `.changes/exempt`, and `debrief.py check --base` (debrief 0.3.0) stops asking those pull requests for a record. The list is read from the base branch, so a pull request can't exempt its own changes, and a code change beside exempt data still needs a record.
entries.try: Which paths in this repo's recent pull requests would belong in .changes/exempt?

changes: The Quality Director can now track test code against source code per repo per week. Once the quality books have `books/volume.csv` (header only to start), `fetch` counts the test and source lines of each watched repo at the head of each complete week's newest push run on the default branch, from the repo's tarball read in memory, and `ingest` books one row per repo and week. `summary` adds `volume`: the week's lines and files and the change since the last booked week. `fetch --since DATE` backfills earlier weeks. It downloads the full source of every watched repo, private ones included, and keeps only the counts.
entries.try: Create books/volume.csv in the quality books, then fetch, ingest and summarize last week's test volume.

changes: New `no-comments` skill deletes the comments a change adds and fixes the code that leaned on them. A `comment-sicko` subagent removes every comment outside a short keep-list (license headers, public API doc comments, constraints from things we cannot change, issue links) and flags the symbols a comment was covering for. You get the fixes, and an offer to turn each "do not remove" note into a type, a test or a check. Adapted from pstack.

A diff that adds a comment to a Python file can now fail a check. `comments.py --base origin/main` lists each added comment and exits 1. A moved comment adds nothing, and a shebang, a tool directive, a license header and a comment with a link always pass. agent-kit's own reliability checklist runs it on every change to a Python file.

beau-mode's rule on comments is stricter: a comment that explains a surprise in our own code is no longer allowed, because the fix is to reshape the code. Opening a PR runs `no-comments` when the diff adds comments.
entries.try: Run /no-comments on this branch's diff.

changes: A private repo's CI can now run on your Mac instead of GitHub-hosted runners. The new local-ci skill runs the repo's `scripts/ci` at each open PR head and the default branch head in a throwaway worktree, and posts the result as the `local-ci` commit status, which the PR's checks list shows. A red run also leaves one PR comment with the end of the log. `local_ci.py install --repo OWNER/NAME=CHECKOUT` sets up a launchd agent that checks every five minutes; `local_ci.py run --pr N` runs one PR now.

Jobs that stay on GitHub Actions (a pull_request_target check, a deploy) can now run locally when GitHub doesn't start them. `local_ci.py fallback --pr N` finds the jobs GitHub finished without starting (no steps, no runner: a spending limit or an outage), runs each one's `scripts/fallback/<job>` from the base branch against the PR's merge commit, and posts `<job> (local fallback)`. A job that ran on GitHub is never replaced, and a fallback marked `# local-ci: explicit`, such as a deploy, runs only when named with `--job`.
entries.try: Move this repo's CI to local-ci and run it on my open PR.

changes: A reliability checklist item's result in a ledger run now comes from an exit code, not from the agent. `receipt.py --run RUN_ID --actor ACTOR --item ID` runs the item's check and appends a `verification` entry with the verdict, the command, the commit and the checklist's hash. A command item runs its own command as the committed checklist states it; a question item takes the command that answers its probe after `--`. The ledger's format is unchanged, so the entry shows in `ledger show` and not in `ledger receipts`.
entries.try: Run the reliability checklist against origin/main and record each item it prints in the ledger run.

changes: A change that breaks an artifact the kit generated in other repos can now list the repos that hold one. `sweep.py BOOKS_DIR --artifact phase-spec` reads the quality books' watched repos through `gh api` and prints each repo with the files it holds (`phase-spec`, `verify-skill` or `review`). `--containing REGEX` keeps only files in the old format, `--at YYYY-MM-DD` reads the repos as they were that day so a past change can be replayed, and `--public-only` names no private repo.

The Authoring a skill playbook has a step for it: list the repos in the PR and open or name an upgrade PR for each. The reliability checklist gains `generated-artifact-format`, which fires on a change to the product scaffold's checker and templates or to the verification skill generator.
entries.try: Run sweep.py on the quality books for review, and tell me which watched repos hold a REVIEW.md.

changes: A change can no longer switch off the checklist item that judges it. `checklist.py` also reads `.agents/checklist.json` as the merge base has it: an item there that matches the diff still prints when the diff removes it, or edits it so that it no longer fires, with a `note:` line saying so. Deleting the whole file does not silence it.
entries.try: Run the reliability checklist against origin/main.

changes: A repo whose tests run under pytest can now have a test record. `quality.py record-junit --junit FILE --out OUT --repo NAME -- pytest --junitxml=FILE` runs pytest, reads the JUnit XML file it wrote and writes the same record `record` writes, so `fetch`, `ingest`, `check` and `summary` book it with no change. A run that pytest cut short, or whose XML file is missing or refused, is recorded as incomplete and red, never missing. Test ids over 1000 characters are shortened with a hash so the books accept them. qualitydirector 0.13.0.
entries.try: Record a pytest run of a repo with quality.py record-junit and check the file passes ingest.

changes: A repo can keep a reliability checklist, `.agents/checklist.json`: the mistakes that already happened there, each with a trigger read from the diff and a check to run. `verify-work` now runs `checklist.py --base REF` before a verdict and gets only the items the change could repeat, each with the line that fired it. A docs change gets no list. A failed item makes the verdict NOT VERIFIED, and one you could not check makes it INCONCLUSIVE.

`correct` sends a mistake that a diff can show to the checklist instead of the rule table. agent-kit's own checklist starts with five items: a books layout change, a phase spec format change, anything under `plugins/`, a `gh` call, and a skill description change.
entries.try: Run the reliability checklist against origin/main and check each item it prints.

changes: `quality.py fetch` no longer silently misses runs in a busy repo. GitHub returns at most 1,000 runs for a listing filtered by date, counting every workflow in the repo. When a watched repo has more than that since `--since`, fetch splits the listing by created date and lists each part, and prints `listing: N runs since DAY are over GitHub's 1000; listed in W windows`. A single day with more than 1,000 runs cannot be split: fetch reports it as `FAILED listing` with the day and both numbers, exits 1, and still fetches what it did list.

A run that GitHub lists twice, because a new run shifted the pages while they were read, is now fetched and counted once (the larger `run_attempt` is kept), and fetch says `listing: run ID was listed twice; kept once`. A listing that comes back short of GitHub's own count is listed once more and reported as `FAILED listing` if it is still short. A repo under the cap makes the same calls and prints the same lines as before. qualitydirector 0.12.0.
entries.try: Run quality.py fetch for the books with --since 30 days ago and tell me whether any listing was split or reported short.

changes: `quality.py summary` now lists a watched repo whose CI has no test recorder. With the job books adopted, a repo with CI runs in the week and no test records appears as `{lifecycle, recorded: false}`: its job and step numbers, and nothing it did not measure. Every listed repo also says `recorded`, so a weekly brief can say which repos have no test records instead of leaving them out.

`summary` now says whether each listed repo is private (`visibility`), and `summary --public-only` leaves private repos out entirely: their entries, rows, test ids and step names, and the skill-use counts. It is the form to share outside the books, and it exits 2 when `books/repos.csv` does not exist. Books without the job books and without `repos.csv` print exactly what they did. qualitydirector 0.11.0.
entries.try: Run the quality summary with --public-only for the latest week and tell me which repos have no test records.

changes: You can now watch private repos beside public ones without the books leaking them. Create `books/repos.csv` (header `seen,repo,github,visibility`) and `quality.py fetch` records what GitHub says about each watched repo (`repo.json`), and `ingest` books each change of visibility (`ingest --only visibility` books only that, and the output says `visibility REPO changed: public -> private` when one changes). A repo counts as public only when its latest row says `public` and it was never private or internal; a failed lookup keeps it private until a later one answers. `check` validates the file and holds it append-only with `--base`.

`quality.py leak-check BOOKS_DIR FILE...` (qualitydirector 0.10.0) reads text files (or `-` for stdin) and exits 1 when they hold a private repo's name as a whole word, or run links, repo slugs, commit shas, test ids, or job and step names that the books hold about one. Run it on a pull request body, commit messages and the diff before pushing work that used the books to a public repo. A pass is not proof: numbers and anything the books do not hold are not matched. Books without `books/repos.csv` behave exactly as before, except that `leak-check` exits 2 for them.
entries.try: Run leak-check on this pull request description against the quality books.

changes: A repo can now hold its pull requests to a change record: `debrief.py check --base origin/main` (debrief 0.2.0) fails when a pull request changes a file outside the bookkeeping files and adds no `.changes/` record, and when a record it added or edited has a problem. A pull request that touches only `ROADMAP.md`, `HUMAN_TASKS.md`, `IDEAS.md`, phase specs, plans, the decision log or `.audit/` needs none.
`--observe` prints what the check would have failed and exits 0, so a repo can watch it for a week before enforcing. agent-kit's own CI now runs it this way on every pull request.
entries.try: Run the debrief pull request check against origin/main in observe mode and tell me what it would fail.

changes: New `debrief` skill closes out work for you: what was done, each claim with the check that ran, the commit, where its output is kept and what stays unchecked, the next items with where each comes from, why now and its impact, and the release note. Work that ships a change keeps this as `.changes/<date>-<slug>.json`, one record per PR.

`debrief.py check` refuses a record whose VERIFIED claim names no kept output, whose evidence path git ignores or doesn't track, or whose next item has no source, reason or impact. `debrief.py show` prints the brief and `debrief.py notes --since DATE` prints release notes from every record, newest first.
beau-mode replies no longer name a next step on its own: each says where it comes from, why now and its impact. Opening a PR writes the change record and its reply carries the brief.
`.changes/` counts as bookkeeping for receipts, so committing a record doesn't make a criterion's receipt stale.
entries.try: /debrief

changes: The weekly Mac job now books skill versions once installed. `weekly-claude-code.sh` takes `--agentfiles-lock FILE` (default: `AGENTFILES_LOCK`, else `$AGENTFILES_HOME/agentfiles.lock`), and `--install` writes the path into the launch agent. Before this the installed job's environment had neither variable, so every row would have been booked with an empty version. Install the job again to pick it up.
The weekly quality brief steps (qualitydirector 0.9.1) no longer say the brief has six sections: they say to keep every section the books' template has, which now includes Skills.

You can now book skill use: `quality.py book-skills BOOKS_DIR` (qualitydirector 0.9.0) reads this machine's Claude Code and Cursor transcripts and appends one row per skill invocation to `books/skill-uses.csv`: week, skill, the agentfiles lock item that installs it and its commit, tool, how it was invoked (typed, named, auto or subagent), and counts of tool calls, tool searches and tool errors over the first 20 tool results after the load. No transcript text is booked or printed, only closed weeks are booked, and a second run adds nothing. Every verdict is `unjudged` for now.

`quality.py check` validates the new book and holds it append-only, and `summary --json` gains `skills` (uses per skill for the week). Both only once `books/skill-uses.csv` exists; without it every command prints what it printed before.
entries.try: Run book-skills with --dry-run against the quality books and tell me how many skill uses it would book.

changes: The weekly Mac job can also book skill use into the quality books. Install it with `weekly-claude-code.sh --install --quality-repo OWNER/NAME` and, after the cost rows are pushed, it runs `quality.py book-skills` on the same logs and pushes the rows to the quality brief branch (opening the pull request when none is open). Without the flag the job does what it did before, and a failure in the new pass never holds back the cost rows.

The Quality Director now has a speed ladder (`references/speed-ladder.md`): the order in which it may propose making a repo's CI faster. Seven rungs (delete, budget, stage, cache, parallelize, select, shard), each opened by values `summary --json` and `audit-ci` print, each with the proof a proposal must show and the question to ask. It proposes from the first open rung only and still changes no workflow.
entries.try: Which speed proposals are open for agent-ledger this week?

changes: You can now run `quality.py audit-ci REPO_DIR [--json]` (qualitydirector 0.7.0) to see, per workflow and job, the CI-speed facts a proposal needs: cancel-in-progress concurrency for pull requests, `timeout-minutes`, dependency caching, a matrix that runs in full on pull requests, and path filters. It only reads the workflow files, writes nothing, and its output is input for a proposal, never an action.
entries.try: Run the Quality Director's audit-ci on this repo and tell me which jobs have no timeout.

changes: A product's goals now say what measures them, what moves them and the first move. The `docs/VISION.md` goals table has Measure, Lever and First move columns, scaffold-product asks for them in the interview and drafts them when it adopts a repo, and a new phase spec has a `**Lever.**` sentence naming which lever of its goal it pulls.

`check-product.py` fails a goal row that leaves Measure, Lever or First move empty, once the goals table has those columns. A table written before them gets a `note:` line and still passes, so no product repo breaks. scaffold-product's "Add measure, lever and first move to the goals" drafts the cells from evidence for you to confirm.
entries.try: Add measure, lever and first move to the goals in docs/VISION.md.

changes: beau-mode now caps fix rounds. In the Bug fix, Feature and Autonomous run playbooks, when the same check still fails after three fixes, the agent stops work on that check and tells you which check, what it tried and why it is stuck. It doesn't skip, loosen or rerun the check, and "don't stop" doesn't lift the cap. A fix that uncovers a different failure doesn't count against it, and other work carries on.

The Bug fix playbook now says what to do when two fixes haven't held: stop patching, go back to the symptom and run root-cause. In fixture runs the agent stopped patching and tested the premise both fixes shared, but didn't run the root-cause skill.
entries.try: make check still fails after my two fixes. Can you sort it out?

changes: `quality.py summary --json` now reports where CI time goes outside the test suite: a `lifecycle` object per repo (run and queue times, time outside the suite counted run by run, slowest and failing steps; a run counts in the week of its first job), from the job books. It appears only once the job books are adopted; without them the output is unchanged.

`quality.py ingest` now books each run's `jobs.json` into `books/jobs.csv` and `books/steps.csv`, and `check` holds both files to rules, once the books have both files. `ingest --only jobs` books just the jobs and steps. Without the two files nothing changes: books written before them check, ingest, fetch and summarize exactly as before.
`interrogate` gives every adversary the repo's `REVIEW.md`, read from the default branch, so a change can't rewrite the guide it is reviewed by. Claude Code Review reads the same file.

A second `interrogate` round on the same scope starts from the first round's verified and dropped findings. Each finding now has a severity: Important, Nit or Pre-existing (it fails on the merge base too, and its fix gets its own PR).
`scaffold-product` adds a starter `REVIEW.md`, and adopt mode drafts one from past review fixes.
entries.try: Interrogate this branch, then interrogate it again after I fix what you find.

changes: `quality.py summary --json` now groups each repo's tests, their cost and their catches by test kind (`unit`, `e2e`, `property`, `differential`) under `by_kind`. Kinds come from an optional hand-edited `books/kinds.csv` (`repo,prefix,kind`, longest dotted prefix wins); books without it are valid and every test is `unit`. `check` validates the file's form only.

`quality.py fetch` now stores what GitHub reports for each run's jobs and steps as `jobs.json`, once the books have a `books/jobs.csv`. Without that file nothing changes. A failed jobs call fails only that run's jobs and never stops its test artifacts.

Every commit an agent writes now says how it was checked, in a `Verified:` git trailer: `receipt <run-id>`, `verify-work`, `tests` or `none <reason>`. The Opening a PR playbook defines the values, and beau-agent and verify-work carry the rule.
`git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Verified,valueonly)'` lists the stamp beside each commit, so unverified commits can be counted.
entries.try: Show me how each commit on this branch was verified.

changes: `quality.py summary --json` now lists, per repo, `caught_on_pr`: the tests that failed in a pull request run that week, with the evidence link for each failure and a count of distinct tests, beside `failed_on_main`. The books and their checks are unchanged.

`check-product.py --receipts` no longer accepts a receipt for a criterion whose text or probe was rewritten afterward, and `receipt.py` records INCONCLUSIVE when an untracked file was present before the probe.

Ticking two boxes in turn, updating `ROADMAP.md` and the other record files, or renaming a spec no longer makes a receipt fail. A receipt whose commit is missing from the clone now says to run the probe again.

A checked spec criterion now has a receipt: a ledger entry saying which probe ran, on which commit, and what came back. verify-work's `scripts/receipt.py` runs the probe and writes it, so the verdict comes from the exit code.
A PR that moves criteria carries the `ledger receipts` table in its Verification section, and the Product phase playbook checks a box only on a VERIFIED receipt.
`check-product.py --receipts <run-id>` fails when a box was checked without a VERIFIED receipt, or when the code changed after the probe ran. Needs agent-ledger 1.1.0 or newer.
entries.try: Run the probe for the next unchecked criterion in this phase and show me its receipt.

changes: A product phase spec is now its ideal state: three levels (Done, Good, Surprising), criteria and anti-criteria with ids (`C1`, `A1`), and the probe that would prove each one false. A person confirms Done and Good before building starts, and the spec stays after the phase is done.

The Product phase playbook works from the spec's failing criteria, runs each probe before and after a change, lists the criteria a PR moves with evidence (`P1-C3`), and adds a feature to a done phase as new unchecked criteria that reopen it. When you reject work whose criteria passed, it adds the missing criterion first.

`check-product.py` checks the new spec: the three levels and a `**Confirmed.**` line, a probe on every criterion and anti-criterion, unique ids, `Evidence:` on every checked box, a confirmation before a phase is Planned, Building, In progress or Gated, and no unchecked box in a Done phase.
Breaking for product repos: specs with an `## Acceptance` checklist fail `check-product.py` until upgraded. scaffold-product has an upgrade mode that converts them in one PR.
entries.try: /scaffold-product upgrade this repo's phase specs to the ideal-state format

changes: New `root-cause` skill finds a bug's root cause from facts instead of from reading the code, for agent-written or unfamiliar code. `rootcause.py` keeps the case (facts against a control, hypotheses, and the matrix between them), says the one next step, refuses a new hypothesis before the tactics are tried or while several survive, and refuses a root cause until exactly one hypothesis explains every fact and an adversarial review on another model has passed it.

`rootcause.py report` writes the evidence, what was ruled out and by which fact, and the layers the agent couldn't reach as infrastructure work. `rootcause.py recheck` reruns each fact's check and fails while a bug-only signal still holds, so a solved case can gate a deploy.
The Bug fix and Perf issue playbooks send the agent to `root-cause` when the code is unfamiliar or two theories have failed.

changes: The weekly quality brief no longer stops in a Claude Code cloud session: it checks GitHub access with a real `gh api` call, not `gh auth status`, which fails there even when access works. It also says what to do when every artifact download is refused.

`qualitydirector` has the weekly quality brief as numbered steps (`references/weekly-brief.md`): fetch the week's CI test records, book them, summarize, write the brief from the books' template with at most three proposals, check, and open one pull request for sign-off.
entries.try: run the weekly quality brief

changes: `quality.py ingest` books the test-run artifacts CI uploads into the quality books (`runs.csv`, the new `failures.csv`, and `tests-weekly.csv`), rejecting any malformed file by name and booking the rest, and it changes nothing the second time you run it.

`quality.py summary --json` gives one weekly object (suite time against the prior four weeks, slowest tests, failures on push, flaky tests, tests added and removed, the 300-second threshold), so a brief copies numbers instead of computing them.
`quality.py record --sha SHA` records the commit you name, so a pull_request run books the PR head instead of GitHub's temporary merge commit.

`quality.py fetch` downloads the test-results artifacts of the repos in the new `books/watched.csv` through `gh`, with GitHub's own account of each run, and `ingest` believes that account for who a run is (repo, commit, event, workflow, start, link) and a recorder file only for what it measured, so a forged or impersonating artifact cannot put a wrong row into the append-only books. Two conflicting files for one run book neither.

`quality.py ingest` and `check` refuse test ids and other cells that a spreadsheet would run or a terminal would obey, cells over 1000 characters, files over 8 MB or 20000 tests, and starts outside 2020 to 2099; one bad file no longer blocks the others.

A test with both an `error` and a `fail` line in one run is booked as `error`. Books layout changes again: a books folder needs `books/watched.csv` (`repo,github,workflow`), and `failed_on_main` is the failures in pushes to the default branch.
The recorder now leaves SIGINT ignored when it starts that way, as plain unittest does, and a test that runs another suite inside itself no longer turns the outer test red.
Books layout changes: `tests-weekly.csv` has `total_ms` where it had `p50_ms`, and a books folder without `failures.csv` fails `check`.

changes: New `qualitydirector` skill records a unittest run as per-test time and outcome (`quality.py record`), so you can see what a repo's suite costs and which tests are slow or failing. A run that is cut short, an empty suite or a module that fails to import counts as a failure, never a green run.
`quality.py check` validates the quality books (`runs.csv` and `tests-weekly.csv`) and, with `--base REF`, fails if a past run row was edited or removed.

changes: Large work item: each unit PR opens as a draft and is marked ready only once its reviews are in, so a merge can't land before its review.
interrogate: an adversary in another tool's CLI runs read-only and non-interactively; for Cursor, `cursor-agent -p --trust --mode ask`, which can't hang on an approval prompt.

changes: A human who approves a charter or answers a gate in their own terminal passes `--typed-by-me`; when an agent types it in, it records the human's words and its own id, and `ledger` refuses an entry with neither.

New Large work item playbook in beau-mode. Multi-PR, unattended or gated work starts with a charter a human approves by its hash, and every decision, gate answer, review and cost goes into the project's ledger, sealed when the run merges.
show-me-your-work records the decision trail with the `ledger` CLI instead of a TSV file, so CI can check that nobody edited it. Install `ledger` with agentfiles or pip.

changes: New `beau-help` skill lists every agent-kit skill and playbook, with how to call each one in your tool.
`beau-help new` shows what changed since you last looked. In Claude Code it also appears once at session start after an update.

changes: beau-mode restates your goal first and carries it into every subagent brief, PR and final reply. It stops when the evidence rules out the change you asked for.
